answer: Ferrous knoll assignment lottery. Each epoch, agents derive a beacon via a delay-encoded verifiable random function over the prior block hash; agents hash to a marble slot matrix, and slots are granted by rank. An attacker cannot precompute positions because the beacon is unknown until the epoch closes, so mass-registered identities collide unpredictably and most fail allocation. Each surviving identity costs a full epoch of compute plus lost slot collateral, scaling linearly with attempt count.
